findings.title: BBC: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
findings.summary_md: The BBC reported that hundreds of French supermarkets had refrigeration units heated by a cyber attack, with some reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros spoiled. More than 100 Cooperative U stores and 180 Intermarche and Netto stores were affected, and Paris prosecutors opened a cybercrime investigation. The report is early news coverage of the campaign that began on October 11.

findings.title: CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 on remote refrigeration controller compromises
findings.summary_md: CERT-FR reported numerous compromises of internet-exposed Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers along with Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb devices. It told operators to remove public exposure, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network, and check the whole configuration, especially defrost ranges. The alert warned that a factory reset alone was insufficient because a compromised device would remain vulnerable and could be compromised again.

findings.title: Irish NCSC advisory on security incidents targeting remote refrigeration controllers
findings.summary_md: Ireland's NCSC warned that attackers had gained unauthorised access to refrigeration controllers directly reachable over the public internet and could view or modify configurations. It listed Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM series and Copeland and Dixell XWEB devices as affected families. Recommended actions included removing direct internet exposure, using a secured VPN for remote access, and reviewing temperature setpoints, defrost schedules, alarm settings, remote access permissions and user accounts.

findings.title: ACDS: Three weeks warning, Europes exposed refrigeration controllers after the French attacks
findings.summary_md: ACDS documented a second wave on November 1 and 2 in which more than a hundred stores across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Estonia, Ireland and Portugal had controllers forced into defrost, with some units reaching 50C. Its mapping showed that three of the five largest exposed AK-SM 800A estates outside France were hit, while half of the world's visible controllers were still online three weeks after the first wave. By November 4 the exploitable remainder in attacked countries was down to about 200 addresses, almost all reachable only through their carrier.

findings.title: Sekoia: The cold chain on fire, unpatched Danfoss controllers exploited
findings.summary_md: Sekoia observed more than 2,700 Danfoss systems exposed worldwide on October 11, about 1,700 of them in France, and said attackers changed temperature settings, defrost cycles and alarm thresholds. Its honeypots logged unauthenticated `read_units` and `xml.cgi` requests from 26 unique IP addresses, password spraying with `12345`, and a November 1 attempt to rename user ID 1 from `178.83.226[.]215` and `37.16.75[.]128`. The report also notes that French authorities attributed the campaign on November 9 to the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh, known behind the CyberAveng3rs persona.

findings.title: Midnight Blue: Multiple remote code execution vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM800A
findings.summary_md: Carlo Meijer of Midnight Blue found six pre-authentication stack-based buffer overflows in AK-SM800A firmware up to and including 5.3.2 in under an hour of manual review. Five sat in `sm_app` web request handlers and one in the `sm_fcgi_app` session-control path, with root code execution demonstrated on 3.3.0 while the bugs remained present in 5.3.2. The authors warned that OS-level access could persist through factory reset and firmware update because the i.MX6 secure boot fuses were unused, and argued for cutting exposure instead of prioritising patches.
